text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Arsenal and Sheffield United at the Emirates Stadium!
A late showing in their last Premier League game saw Arsenal come from 2-0 down to draw with Chelsea at Stamford Bridge to maintain their unbeaten start in the competition (W6 D3).
They're looking to close the gap to Tottenham back to two points again at the top of the table and come into this game on the back of a 2-1 victory over Sevilla in the Champions League on Tuesday.

It couldn't be a bigger contrast to their opponents, as United prop up the table with just a solitary point to their name from a draw with Everton, having lost their other eight outings in the Premier League.

They're still looking for their first victory in any competition this season and will be looking to turn things around after losing their last five matches on the bounce, conceding 17 times in that run and scoring just two.
Mikel Arteta makes five changes to the side that beat Sevilla on Tuesday, as Kiwior, Zinchenko, Smith Rowe, Havertz and Nketiah are all brought in.
Gabriel, Tomiyasu, Odegaard and Jorginho all start on the bench, while Gabriel Jesus is out after picking up a hamstring injury in that game.
There are just two changes by Paul Heckingbottom from their defeat to Manchester United last weekend.
Slimane and Brewster are both brought in to make their first starts of the season.
Archer drops to the bench, where they're boosted by the return of Baldock after a calf injury.
Oli McBurnie is out with a groin injury sustained in that match.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Hamer gets the game under way for United!
Arsenal win it quickly after the kick-off and they're looking to make a bright start here.
They work it upfield well down their left, but Martinelli just can't pick out a cross into the box.
It's patient play from the hosts as they keep United penned back in their own half.
Zinchenko and Martinelli link up well once more, but again, the cross is blocked.
The space opens up for Rice just outside the D, so he decides to try his luck.
Robinson is in the right place to block it, and then he reacts quickly to stop Nketiah from pouncing onto the loose ball.
Arsenal are unbeaten in 36 Premier League home games against promoted side (W31 D5), with their last such defeat coming against Newcastle United in November 2010.
Saliba trips over the ball and Brewster picks his pocket before Slimane takes over down the left.
He cushions it into Hamer's path, but White gets across to dispossess him before he can get it out of his feet.
Nketiah initially does well to hold the ball up against Trusty, but then goes down in the box.
The defender got the last touch though, so Arsenal win a corner, which is whipped over everyone in the six-yard box.
United try to pass their way out from the back, but when McAtee runs into Zinchenko, he tries to restart.
He gifts it to Havertz, but luckily for him, Norwood is there on the cover.
Zinchenko makes a supporting run into the box, and when he's picked out by Martinelli, he looks to pull it back to Nketiah.
Norwood slides in and gets enough on it to help it into Foderingham's gloves.
Arsenal are still dominating possession here, but they're having to be patient.
The visitors are pressing high and making it difficult for the hosts to get into the final third.
Hamer's free-kick is plucked out of the air by Raya, and he goes long, setting Martinelli straight on the counter.
He can't get past Bogle to have a shot, so he lays it off to Saka, but a heavy first touch shows too much of it to Robinson.

text: The Blades are moving the ball a lot quicker when they win it back now, and Hamer goes for the big switch out to McAtee.
He cuts inside to lose Zinchenko, but there's no one in the box to get on the end of his shot.
It's spread out to McAtee once more, but he quickly loses out this time.
United flood back into their own half, and Arsenal are back to knocking it around in front of the visitors, trying to find some space.
Bogle kicked through Martinelli, giving away a foul, and the Brazilian stays down.
He's receiving treatment on his ankle, but he'll be able to carry on.
NKETIAH SCORES! The home fans were starting to get frustrated, and Arsenal do something about it! It's worked down the right, through White, Havertz and Saka, who squares it into Rice.
He has a quick glance up to spot Nketiah in space near the penalty spot and curls a low cross into him.
He takes it around Trusty before slotting past Foderingham.
1-0 Arsenal!
The visitors just don't close Rice down when it's played into him, and it gives him time to pick out a good low cross between the defenders.
Sheff United are back to pressing high upfield instead of sitting back like they'd started to do in the last few minutes.
Arsenal are looking for a quick-fire second, but they're being put under some pressure at the moment.
Robinson spots Brewster's run, but Nketiah quickly rushes in to close him down and blocks the pass.
He can't make anything of it though as it rolls out for a goal-kick.
It's better from United here as Slimane threads it forward for Thomas, who gets a yard on White.
He tries to pull it back from the byline, but his cross is blocked by Saliba as a belated flag goes up.
Saliba goes long over the top, and it's Zinchenko who makes the run off the back of the last man.
He brings it down on his chest, but Trusty recovers well to slide in and stop him from getting a shot away.
Thomas decides to go for a more direct route this time, lifting it over the top towards Slimane.
He has Saliba tight to his back though, and can't do anything when he brings it down.
Kiwior is allowed to carry the ball a long way, and he threads it forward for Saka.
His intended flick doesn't come off, but Havertz does come away with the ball, only to run into Souza.
GOOD SAVE! Smith Rowe and Saka link up well down the left before it's cushioned into Martinelli just inside the box.
His first touch gets him away from Bogle before he fires a shot at the near post, but Foderingham pushes it away.
CHANCE! Martinelli has the beating of McAtee and he fizzes a low cross into the box from the byline.
Smith Rowe is unmarked but slips as he takes the shot.
It loops into the air, and Trusty heads it out for a corner.
Arsenal are upping the pressure here, and United just can't get on the ball at the moment.
The hosts want a second goal before the break and are pushing forward with real intent.
Nketiah fouls Robinson, and Foderingham is urged to go long with his free-kick.
He clips it to the edge of the box where Norwood is waiting, but he can't bring it under control.
HALF-TIME: ARSENAL 1-0 SHEFFIELD UNITED.
Nketiah's strike gives Arsenal a 1-0 lead over Sheffield United at half-time.
It took the hosts a long time to open up their opponents, with the Blades dropping deep to defend their own box.
Eventually, they managed to get in behind, with Rice curling a lovely low cross into Nketiah, who made no mistake with a confident finish.
Martinelli forced Foderingham into a good save at his near post minutes before the break, while United have struggled to get their forwards into the game.
Arteta's frustration in the first 25 minutes was clear to see as his team struggled to get into the final third, but their patience paid off.
They finished the half strongly, and he'll want them to pick up where they left off.
Heckingbottom's game plan worked up until the lapse in concentration for the goal.
Since then, they've struggled to get out of their own half, but they know they need to take more risks to get them back into this.
Arsenal get us back under way for the second half!
It's Arsenal with all of the possession in the opening exchanges here.
The Blades are once again dropping deep to close off any space ahead of them.
NKETIAH SCORES AGAIN! He won the corner which was whipped into the six-yard box by Saka.
Foderingham has White and Bogle in front of him and stretches awkwardly to get a glove on it.
Nketiah reacts quickly to get onto the loose ball and rifles it into the top right corner of the net.

events.action: rifles it into the top right corner

text: United are claiming the keeper was impeded, but after a quick VAR check, the goal stands! 2-0 Arsenal!
The goalkeeper didn't cover himself in glory from the initial corner, but VAR is looking to see if White blocked him from reaching Nketiah's strike.
They see it as a coming together between the players, and the onfield decision stands.
Martinelli is down after being bundled over by Bogle, and it looks like he landed awkwardly on his ankle.
He receives treatment, but is okay to carry on.
It's wonderful play from Saka as he drags Thomas out of position before spinning to try and slip it through to Smith Rowe.
Robinson reads it well though, and makes an important interception.
HAT-TRICK! Martinelli dinks it over Bogle to pick out Smith Rowe, and United are slow to close him down.
He lays it off to Nketiah, who takes on the shot from the edge of the D, firing it over Robinson as he ducks to try and block the shot.

text: Foderingham is stretching, but can't stop it from nestling into the net.
3-0 Arsenal!
Smith Rowe gets the shout from Nketiah, and tees him up for the hat-trick goal.
The visitors are making a double change in response to that third goal.
Brewster, who has struggled to get into the game, goes off for Archer.
And Slimane makes way, with Osborn on in his place.
He's only been on the field for a minute, but Osborn clips the back of Havertz's heels and is shown the first booking of the game.
GOOD SAVE! Robinson bundles the ball away from Havertz, but only gets it as far as Martinelli on the left.
He clips it to the edge of the box where White meets it first time.
His swerving shot is pushed away by Foderingham.
It's better from the visitors as they manage to push Arsenal back into their own box.
Archer looks to Thomas down the left, but he's dispossessed before he can pick out a cross.
Arsenal are making a double change now.
White is going off for Tomiyasu.
And Martinelli makes way as he's replaced by Trossard.
It looks like Rice has overhit the pass, but Tomiyasu manages to scoop it back from the byline.
Nketiah is waiting in the middle to get another chance, but Norwood just beats him to it.
Bogle has his arms all over Trossard as the Belgian tries to cut inside and he's booked for it.
There's another double change for United now.
Bogle, who has just been booked, goes off for Baldock.
And Fleck is brought on for McAtee.
And Saka is taken off, with Nelson on in his place.
Arsenal are also making another double swap.
Smith Rowe is replaced by Vieira.
Arsenal are keeping the ball well here as they patiently try to draw the Blades out once more.
They're moving it from left to right and back again, dragging their opponents across the field.
CHANCE! Trossard gets the better of Baldock, but his cross is headed away by Robinson.
It bounces kindly for Tomiyasu on the edge of the box, but he fizzes his low shot wide.
Nketiah has scored his first Premier League hat-trick, and is the first Englishman to do so in the competition for Arsenal since Theo Walcott against West Brom in May 2015.
It's a lovely throughball from Trossard to pick out Nketiah's run off the back of the defender.
Trusty reads it well and gets across to put a toe in to take it away from him just in time.
United are back to dropping deep inside their own half here and aren't closing Arsenal down as quickly as they were before.
The Gunners are still very comfortable in possession.
The final roll of the dice by Heckingbottom sees One come on for Hamer.
Baldock gave the ball away and Norwood slid in to bring Vieira down right on the line of the box.
The home fans are asking for a penalty, but play is allowed to continue.
VAR is having a look at this though...
PENALTY TO ARSENAL! The referee is asked to go over to the monitor.
It was a poor challenge from Norwood, who slid in to catch the substitute on his heel with his studs.
After a long look, the referee comes back on to point to the spot.
Norwood also goes into the referee's book for the tackle.
VIEIRA SCORES! Cool as you like from the man who won the penalty! Foderingham dives to his right and can only watch as Vieira slides it straight down the middle of the goal to make it 4-0 to Arsenal!
Arsenal's last change sees Elneny come on for Rice.
We're into the first of 10 added minutes here, and the Blades are mounting a rare attack.
Arsenal are staying compact, and though Norwood manages to slide a throughball into Souza, he can't get past Kiwior.
United are making a late show here as Souza slides it through Tomiyasu's legs before winning a corner off Saliba.
The resulting set-piece is too close to Raya though, and the keeper plucks it out of the air.
After a good spell of possession, Souza sloppily gifts the ball to Havertz, who instantly looks to Nketiah.
He drives into the box, but the Brazilian recovers well to prevent a shot.
TOMIYASU SCORES! The resulting corner causes all sorts of problems in the Sheff United box as it's flicked on by Elneny at the near post.
Kiwior is on the ground which actually helps it on its way to Tomiyasu, and he readjusts quickly to volley his shot into the near top corner.

events.action: volley his shot into the near top corner

text: 5-0 Arsenal!
There is a quick VAR check on the goal to make sure there wasn't a handball by an Arsenal player on its way into the net.
The check comes up clean, and the goal stands!
Arsenal are happy to just keep the ball now as they wait for the end of the game.
There are only a couple of minutes left, and that last goal knocked any fightback out of the visitors.
CHANCE! Nelson flicks it past One and manages to pick out Zinchenko, who cushions it into Havertz.
He takes the shot first time, looking to catch Foderingham out at his near post, but he hits the side netting.
FULL-TIME: ARSENAL 5-0 SHEFFIELD UNITED.
Nketiah's hat-trick helps Arsenal cruise to a 5-0 victory over Sheffield United.
The visitors actually frustrated the Gunners for the first 25 minutes or so, but Nketiah got his first goal with a smart finish over the keeper.

He wrapped up the game within 15 minutes of the second half starting, latching onto Foderingham's poor clearance to rifle in his second before earning the match ball with a wonderful strike from the edge of the D.
Vieira won a late penalty which he then coolly converted before Tomiyasu rounded off the scoring in stoppage time with a fine finish following a corner.
That win moves Arsenal up into second place, now just two points behind Spurs.
Next up for them is a trip to West Ham in the EFL Cup in midweek.
The Blades are now the only team in the Premier League without a win to their name as they stay bottom.
They host Wolves next weekend.
That's all for today, goodbye!
